extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: ChartQA is a large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning. It covers 9,608 human-written questions as well as 23,111 questions generated from human-written chart summaries. The benchmark consists of 20,882 charts curated from four different online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD) to ensure variety in visual styles and topics. The dataset focuses on complex reasoning questions involving visual references and logical/arithmetic operations.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.publisher: York University, Nanyang Technological University, Salesforce Research
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Pew, only chart images were crawled since underlying data tables are not available. For the other three sources, underlying data tables, metadata (title, chart type), SVG file, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and additional QA pairs were machine-generated from human-written Statista summaries using a T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, underlying data tables are not available, so only chart images were crawled.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts crawled from Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). Human-authored questions collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Machine-generated questions derived from human-written Statista summaries.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For machine-generated questions, a heuristic was used to filter invalid questions: questions whose answers cannot be found in the chart data table were filtered out. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions. Bounding box information was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two main annotation procedures: (1) Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk where crowdworkers provided two types of questions per chart: compositional (involving at least two mathematical/logical operations like sum, difference, average) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, length of graphical marks). For each chart, two questions with answers were provided, then answered by another annotator for verification. If answers matched exactly, considered correct; otherwise manually checked. (2) Machine-generated QA pairs: Two T5 models were fine-tuned on SQuAD—one for answer extraction and another for answer-aware question generation—and applied to human-written Statista chart summaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Exact match agreement between crowd workers was 61.04%. Manual checking on 500 random samples showed higher agreement of 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations. For machine-generated questions, manual analysis of 1,250 QA pairs found 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct given the chart.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotators per question for human-authored QA pairs (one provides Q&A, one verifies)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers selected with acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000. Workers were further filtered by a pre-test to select the best qualified workers. Compensation was $0.6 USD per task (estimated 3-5 minutes per task), based on US minimum wage of $7.25/hour. Annotations were anonymized.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model fine-tuned on SQuAD for answer extraction and question generation; CRAFT model for text recognition; ChartOCR adapted for data extraction; Mask R-CNN with Resnet-101 backbone for visual feature extraction
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors acknowledge that models can be abused to mislead the public about chart contents and implications. They cannot guarantee that model outputs will be correct all the time.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Evaluation reveals challenges in answering complex reasoning questions, especially those requiring nested operations. Current models cannot effectively handle nested mathematical/logical operations. Input representations do not fully capture chart structure. Performance of models decreases when gold table is not given, suggesting limitations of automatic data extraction. Pie charts have higher data extraction errors as they are less common in the dataset. Evaluation metrics for chart data extraction do not take extracted textual tokens into consideration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing splits are provided. ChartQA-H: 3,699 charts/7,398 questions (training), 480/960 (validation), 625/1,250 (test). ChartQA-M: 15,474/20,901 (training), 680/960 (validation), 987/1,250 (test). Use case: benchmark for chart question answering with visual and logical reasoning.
